chunks: Eat from the bird that has a gizzard for it, but no claw for it.
He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the birds of the water, so he said: Similar to that.

key_terms.طير الماء: Water birds — aquatic birds such as ducks, herons, and other waterfowl
key_terms.قانصة: Gizzard — the muscular stomach found in grain-eating birds, a sign of a halal bird
key_terms.مخلب: Talon/claw — the sharp curved claw of a predatory bird (bird of prey), a sign of a haram bird

ai.seo_question: How do you identify which birds are permissible (halal) to eat in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a jurisprudential criterion for identifying permissible (halal) birds: the presence of a gizzard combined with the absence of talons/claws. This ruling is extended to apply equally to aquatic birds when the narrator inquires about them. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, a gizzard is a sign of grain-eating birds (permitted), while talons indicate predatory birds of prey (forbidden).
